delivers fully integrated automation solutions nationwide that optimize performance, energy efficiency, and reliability across HVAC, lighting, power monitoring, and mission-critical systems. Leveraging advanced technologies - including Allen-Bradley PLCs, Ignition SCADA, and Delta DDC systems - we combine deep technical expertise with field-tested execution to deliver precise, scalable, and high-performance solutions.

About The Role

The Project Coordinator

is a project delivery support role designed to assist Project Managers in the successful execution of data center controls construction projects. This position provides administrative coordination, documentation management, schedule tracking, financial support, and cross-functional communication to ensure projects are executed efficiently and in accordance with company standards.

The Project Coordinator contributes to project success by maintaining documentation workflows, supporting cost and schedule tracking, coordinating vendors and field teams, and assisting with internal and client communication.

This is an onsite role in Irving, TX.

Key Responsibilities

Project Coordination & Execution

Support Project Managers in coordinating day-to-day execution of data center controls projects.
Assist in updating project schedules, track milestones, and identify potential risks or delays.
Coordinate internal teams, subcontractors, and vendors to support timely project delivery.
Assist with mobilization planning, site access documentation, and workforce logistics.
Support preparation of project status reports and internal dashboards.

Documentation & Controls

Manage document control processes, including submittals, RFIs, change logs, drawings, contracts, and closeout documents.
Maintain accurate and organized project files in project management, accounting, and document systems.
Track submittals and RFIs to ensure timely processing and follow-up.
Prepare meeting agendas, capture minutes, and track follow-up actions.
Update project management systems with current status notes, documentation, and dependencies.

Client & Stakeholder Support

Assist Project Managers with communication workflows and documentation required by clients.
Support coordination between engineering, procurement, accounting, and field teams.
Maintain action item logs and ensure timely follow-through on assigned tasks.

Cost, Billing & Administrative Support

Assist with budget tracking, cost coding, and invoice support.
Track purchase orders, subcontractor pay applications, vendor invoices, and material receipts.
Support preparation and tracking of change orders and associated documentation.
Coordinate with accounting to ensure accurate billing and job cost reporting.
Monitor committed costs versus budget and escalate discrepancies to the Project Manager.

Field &

Closeout

Support

Track daily reports and assist in compiling project progress documentation.
Support workforce planning documentation and field reporting processes.
Assist in tracking punch-list items and project closeout requirements.
Help assemble O&M manuals and closeout packages.
Archive project records in accordance with company standards.

Qualifications

Required

2+ years of project coordination or project administration experience in construction or related industries.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
High attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel required).
Experience with project management or accounting platforms.

Preferred

Experience supporting MEP, controls, building automation, or data center construction projects.
Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Business, or related field.
Basic understanding of construction financial processes including budgets, cost codes, and change orders.
Experience with platforms such as Procore, Monday.com, Sage Intacct, Foundation, or similar systems.

Physical Requirements

Sit and/or stand for extended periods (typically 6-8 hours per day) while performing computer-based tasks and facility support tasks.
Use hands and fingers to operate standard office equipment, including computers, keyboards, mice, telephones, scanners and printers.
Occasionally stand, walk, bend, stoop, or reach to access filing cabinets, retrieve documents, or attend meetings.
Lift, carry, push, or pull light objects and materials weighing up to 20-25 pounds (e.g., boxes of files or office supplies).
Have sufficient vision (with or without correction) to read computer screens, printed documents, and small print; and sufficient hearing to communicate effectively by phone and in person.
Work in a typical indoor office environment with moderate noise levels from office equipment, conversations, and occasional interruptions.

new_jobs.description:
About Judi Health

Judi Health is a health technology company providing benefit administration solutions to employers, unions, health plans, and government entities. Judi Health replaces fragmented, outdated systems with the industry's first Unified Claims Processing™ architecture, seamlessly consolidating pharmacy and medical benefit administration on a single, secure platform. By delivering true price transparency, eliminating unnecessary middleman fees, and leveraging advanced AI-powered care delivery, Judi Health helps clients achieve unprecedented operational efficiency and service levels.

At Judi Health, we're deploying the infrastructure our country needs to deliver the healthcare we all deserve. We are the intelligence platform powering benefits plans for millions of Americans and proudly leading the next generation of care. To learn more, visit www.judi.health.

Location: Hybrid 3 days (offices in NYC, Denver, CO and Charlotte, NC area)

Position Summary

Lead Judi Rx’s Underwriting Data Analyst team in the day-to-day operations in support of underwriting for both new business opportunities and recontracting of current clients. Manage, train, and mentor the Underwriting Data Analyst team members in all facets of their roles, as well as act as the first POC and SME for all data-related questions for the greater Underwriting department. Directly contribute to and provide oversight over the Underwriting Data Analyst team’s infrastructure including maintaining existing functionality and leading the development of new features.

Position Responsibilities

Collect, clean, process, and analyze potential and current clients’ pharmaceutical data – using SQL, Python, R, and MS Excel as appropriate – to support the Underwriting and Sales teams in the acquisition of new business and retention of current clients
Thoroughly understand internal and external data fields, identify patterns of data irregularities, and improve data quality and intake
Coordinate with relevant parties regarding any data ambiguity and request any additional data elements that may be required or beneficial for analysis
Troubleshoot and customize infrastructure code in SQL, Python, and R to diagnose and solve data or process issues
Create custom code in SQL, Python, and R for improved or entirely new functionality in support of ad hoc requests and to further the development of our growing infrastructure
Manage the development of new analyses, reporting, and process enhancements in support of pricing models for new and existing products
Provide ad-hoc analytics support to the Underwriting team for the successful completion of all bid opportunities
Provide analytics support to the Pricing, Clinical, Account Management, and Implementation teams to facilitate client transitions
Collaborate with Leadership Team and other business functions (sales, marketing, account management) to develop and maintain internal underwriting, financial modeling, and financial reporting system infrastructure and SOPs
Train and on-board new hires in Underwriting data, tools, and processes
Manage a team of Underwriting Data Analysts as direct reports
Manage the Underwriting Data Analyst work queue and assignments
Provide QA review of all ad hoc analyses and custom views for both internal and external reporting purposes
Establish and maintain team documentation on processes, procedure, and best practices

Required Qualifications

Undergraduate bachelor’s degree, with record of strong academic performance in Statistics, Economics, Finance, Business, Computer Science, or a quantitative social science
5+ years of proven experience in data analysis, such as financial analysis, actuarial services, accounting, pricing & underwriting
1+ year of experience in managing direct reports
1+ year of experience working with pharmaceutical claims data
Expertise in SQL for data transformation and data analysis with strong coding hygiene and documentation practices
Proficiency in Python and R
Working knowledge of ETL fundamentals and experience working with cloud-based data warehouses
Experience working with structured and unstructured data
Track record of leading cross-functional initiatives, driving high performance, meeting deadlines, and executing on deliverables
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple complex projects simultaneously under a frequently shifting work queue
Extremely flexible, highly organized, and able to shift priorities easily
Attention to detail & commitment to delivering high-quality work products

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree, with record of strong academic performance in Statistics, Economics, Finance, Business, Computer Science, or a quantitative social science
Knowledge of medical claims data
Knowledge of Tableau
Knowledge of and passion for improving the health care industry

Nothing in this position description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

This range represents the low and high end of the anticipated base salary range. The actual base salary will depend on several factors such as: experience, knowledge, and skills, and location of the job.

New York, NY Salary Range: $150,800 USD - $188,500 USD

Denver, CO Salary Range: $138,000 USD - $172,500 USD

new_jobs.title: GIS Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Description

"

As a GIS Analyst with AMS, your office is wherever data meets the real world. Whether mapping utility corridors in urban centers or analyzing terrain in remote forests, you play a critical role in supporting safe and efficient utility operations. As an AMS GIS Analyst, you will transform spatial data into actionable insights that help keep the lights on and communities safe.

Some of the most important characteristics of an AMS GIS Analyst are attention to detail, analytical thinking, and the ability to communicate complex spatial information clearly. You are accountable for advancing a culture of safety and excellence while providing quality and value to our customers and clients.

The pay range for this position is from $20.00 to $30.00 per hour, contingent upon relevant education, experience, and industry-specific certifications. This specified range is determined by the tier associated with the job posting. However, should the employee be classified under a different tier, the compensation may fall outside the stated range.

WHAT WE OFFER:

Industry competitive pay
Medical/Health/Dental/Vision/VOYA/Paid Holidays/EAP eligibility on day one of employment (Full-Time Employees)
401K, Vacation Accrual, life insurance, long-term disability eligibility first of the month after 3 months of service
Sick Time eligibility on day 90 of employment
Weekly paychecks and direct deposit
Participation in the Employee Referral Program (must meet eligibility requirements)
Boot and clothing program (company funded, if applicable)
Ongoing training and assistance with obtaining industry certifications

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Analyze and interpret spatial data to support utility vegetation management (UVM) programs and infrastructure planning
Create, maintain, and update GIS databases, maps, and dashboards
Perform spatial analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities
Respond to data inquiries & support field crews and arborists with reports, maps, spreadsheets, etc.
Manage specialized databases and spreadsheets, entering data and generating reports with proficiency in Microsoft Excel
Collaborate with field teams to integrate GPS-collected data into GIS systems
Generate reports and visualizations to support decision-making and regulatory compliance
Ensure data accuracy and consistency across platforms and projects
Support QA/QC processes for spatial data and field-collected information
Assist in developing and maintaining automated workflows using GIS tools and scripting
Travel may be required for field data collection or coordination with field teams

WHAT YOU NEED TO HAVE:

1-2 years of experience working with GIS software and databases, including ESRI Suite
Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree in Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or a related field
Proficiency in GIS software (e.g., ArcGIS, QGIS)
Experience with spatial data formats and coordinate systems
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to work independently,manage multiple tasks, and show attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Basic programming/scripting knowledge (e.g., Python, SQL) is a plus
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel if needed

WHAT WOULD BE AMAZING TO HAVE:

Experience in utility or environmental GIS applications
Familiarity with GPS data collection tools and mobile GIS apps
Certification such as GISP or Esri Technical Certification
UVM Experience
Bi-Lingual (English/Spanish) a plus

Working Environment

Primarily office-based with occasional fieldwork; may involve travel to utility corridors or remote locations. Work may include exposure to various weather conditions and terrain. Reasonable accommodation, if available, may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.

Physical

Must be able to sit or stand for extended periods, operate a computer and related equipment, and occasionally travel to field sites. Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. and walk on uneven terrain may be required for field data collection.

Company Overview

Arbormetrics (AMS) is a leading provider of vegetation and asset management consulting services to the utility industry. Successful professionals at AMS have come from a variety of backgrounds, including: GIS, geography, environmental science, forestry, natural resource management, and more. For more information visit our website www.arbormetrics.com

Applicants must pass a pre-employment drug test and a criminal background check.

All candidates must possess a valid driver's license and have a good driving record.

AMS is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. EOE/AA : Minority/Female/ Vets/ Disabled.

Individuals with a disability who desire a reasonable accommodation can contact the ADA Coordinator by calling 1-833-222-3066. We partner with the Department of Homeland Security/U.S. Customs and Immigration Service to e-Verify all newly hired employees.

"

new_jobs.title: Environmental Scientist II
new_jobs.description:
Welcome to Verdantas, where innovation meets sustainability, and your career finds purpose!

At Verdantas, we’re redefining environmental consulting and sustainable engineering through our use of cutting-edge modeling and digital technology and our genuine commitment to people. Our work spans high-growth sectors like water resources, resilient land use, energy transformation, and civil infrastructure.

Our commitment to excellence, across more than 90 offices, is championed by a team of over 2,000 experts, scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists, embedded in a people-focused culture, prioritizing the well-being of our employees, clients, and the communities we serve. We partner with clients to deliver smart, data-driven solutions to complex environmental and infrastructure challenges. We don’t just solve problems; we help shape a more sustainable future.

Join a people-first culture that values your well-being, empowers your growth, and amplifies your impact. At Verdantas, your career goes beyond the expected, and your work helps build a better world.

Ready to shape the future of resilient communities?

Our growing South Area team is seeking a motivated, talented Staff Scientist II
for our Environmental Assessment and Remediation (EAR) practice
.

Our South Area EAR practice focuses on site assessment/remedial investigations and design, environmental regulatory compliance and support, feasibility studies, emerging contaminants, and property transaction due diligence for clients in industrial, power, water, and government end markets. The Staff Scientist II will collaborate with diverse project teams of engineers and environmental professionals to execute and deliver solutions to complex environmental challenges for clients throughout the South Area and across the greater Verdantas footprint.

What You'll Do

Understand, protect, and promote our empathetic, people-focused culture in all aspects of the business
Work in a combination of office and outdoor environments. When in an outdoor environment, the employee is subject to walking distances on uneven terrain while wearing personal protective equipment, including but not limited to work boots with safety toes, high-visibility safety vests, long pants, long-sleeve shirts, and hard hats, along with exposure to varying weather conditions typical of Florida and limited heavy lifting
Outdoor work may require overnight travel, weekend work, out-of-town assignments, early morning starts (before 7:00 a.m.), and/or late departures (after 6:00 p.m.) in accordance with OSHA regulations
Report to the office when not performing field work
Perform field tasks and maintain field notes as assigned by project managers and senior technical staff
Conduct drilling oversight and logging of soil borings, monitoring wells, and soil vapor points
Collect groundwater, soil, sediment, air, and surface water samples for laboratory analysis according to regulatory and company standard operating procedures
Enter collected data into report format using applicable software and company formatting guidelines
Assist in preparing regulatory submittals, such as permit applications and work plans
Prepare technical reports documenting project findings, conclusions, and recommendations
Operate and maintain remediation systems
Troubleshoot equipment issues associated with remediation systems, including groundwater and soil screening equipment before and/or during field work events
Operate a variety of field vehicles, from SUVs to full-size trucks, including towing, following completion of required Verdantas training
Prepare project-specific Health and Safety Plans (HASPs)
Prepare maps and other illustrations for data interpretation and presentation
Maintain Excel databases associated with regulatory compliance activities
Apply basic knowledge of federal, state, and local regulatory requirements and programs

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Geology, Environmental Science, Environmental, Civil, or Chemical Engineering, or a related discipline
3-5 years of relevant experience
Strong problem-solving skills and a positive, can-do attitude
Flexibility and self-motivation, including a willingness to learn new skills
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively interact with clients, regulators, contractors, property owners, and project team members
Basic knowledge of federal, state, and local regulatory requirements and programs
Experience with AutoCAD, ArcGIS Pro, and other mapping software is a plus, but not required
40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER training is a plus, but not required
Must possess a valid driver's license
U.S. citizenship or permanent residency is required for access to Department of Defense (DoD) facilities
Access to a cell phone with internet connectivity

Salary Range

Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications of the candidate as it relates to the position description

Essential Job Duties

The
Sheth plant evolutionary ecology lab
in the
Department of Plant and Microbial Biology
at
North Carolina State University
(Raleigh, NC) is currently seeking field technician to participate in an NSF -funded study (
https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2220928&HistoricalAwards=false
) under the direction of Dr. Seema Sheth and in collaboration with Drs. Susana Wadgymar (Davidson College), Jill Anderson (University of Georgia), Megan DeMarche (University of Georgia), and Emily Josephs (Michigan State University).

The project combines approaches from evolutionary biology, field ecology, and population genomics in a broadly distributed native plant species (
Chamaecrista fasciculata
, Fabaceae) to forecast population dynamics range-wide under climate change. The technician will be part of a dynamic, dedicated, and engaged research group as well as a member of a multidisciplinary and multi-institution collaborative group that includes Botanic Garden and conservation professionals.

The successful candidate will contribute to a collaborative study of eco-evolutionary responses to climate in the partridge pea,
Chamaecrista fasciculata
, an annual legume that grows in disturbed habitats in central and eastern North America. The technician’s primary responsibilities involve collaborating with the PIs and other researchers to establish and maintain a large common garden experiment and to collect data from ~6,000 transplanted seeds at Mason Farm Biological Reserve in Chapel Hill, NC. This work includes preparing seeds for planting, planting seeds, setting up the garden infrastructure, building open-top chambers, collecting data on traits and fitness, entering data, maintenance tasks in the garden (e.g., weeding), processing samples in the lab, and communicating with Dr. Sheth and other team members. The technician will also have opportunities to train and mentor undergraduate students and work with graduate students.

new_jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Project Manager
plans, coordinates, and oversees safe, efficient environmental field work in accordance with Field Work Orders (FWOs), company procedures, client expectations, and regulatory requirements. This role connects Project Management, Field Operations, clients, vendors, contractors, and field personnel; ensures work is properly scheduled, staffed, equipped, documented, and completed; and provides field leadership and support as needed.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Report writing
Lead tasks on more complex projects
Client interaction
Regulatory interaction
Troubleshooting
Budgeting/costing projects
Participate in field activities
Prepare FWOs, schedules, drawings, permits, sampling requirements, site information, and other project documents before field work begins.
Schedule and coordinate qualified personnel, vehicles, equipment, materials, lodging, and vendors;
Perform or lead environmental sampling, monitoring, investigation, remediation, well installation, and related field services in accordance with project and regulatory requirements.
Direct employees, temporary staff, and contractors; assign work, provide training and coaching, monitor performance, and reinforce accountability and professionalism.
Maintain a safety-first work environment, verify required training and PPE, report incidents and unsafe conditions, and stop or delay work when necessary.
Coordinate waste pickups and disposal; prepare, track, and retain manifests and supporting records through final disposition.
Ensure timely submission of FWOs, field notes, sampling records, photographs, manifests, and other required documentation.
Communicate project status, field conditions, deviations, equipment or personnel concerns, and recommended solutions to appropriate stakeholders.

ACCOUNTABILITY & PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Success is measured by safe, well-planned, adequately staffed and equipped field work that meets project requirements, is documented promptly, and is completed with minimal avoidable delays. The role is expected to anticipate needs, resolve issues, maintain an accurate field calendar, and keep project progressing.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Required

High school diploma or GED and relevant environmental, construction, industrial, or field-services experience.
Valid driver’s license
Ability to develop and/or execute FWOs, collect and document field information accurately, and communicate effectively with employees, contractors, clients, and Project Managers.
Ability to work outdoors, operate or learn field equipment safely, manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and work independently or as part of a team.

Preferred

Associate or bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, engineering, construction management, project management, or a related field.
40hr HAZWOPER certification;
OCC Environmental Consultant, AST/UST Remover
ASB/LBP Licenses
Experience with environmental sampling or remediation, field equipment, waste manifests, project coordination, and leading crews or contractors.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

Project coordination, scheduling, organization, prioritization, and problem solving.
Clear written and verbal communication with employees, clients, vendors, contractors, and regulators.
Leadership, coaching, accountability, and collaborative decision-making.
Environmental sampling, field documentation, basic equipment troubleshooting, and recognition of unusual or unsafe conditions.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to learn OES scheduling, project-management, documentation, and communication systems.

WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Company Description

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Job Description

Hybrid-based position in our Syracuse office.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your excellence in an inclusive, collaborative, and empowering community? Are you excited about joining a company that strives to make a difference – for its employees, clients, and society? Are you motivated by creating sustainable change that benefits society and nature?

If this sounds like you, or you’re curious to learn more, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our Environment & Health team and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

We invite you to bring your environmental consulting experience into play as you support provide technical and project leadership for environmental investigation and remediation projects in the New York area. In this position, the selected candidate will lead and support multidisciplinary teams working closely with Professional Engineers (PEs), Professional Geologists (PGs), Licensed Site Remediation Professionals (LSRPs) and other technical specialists.

As a senior member of the team, you will apply your technical expertise and professional judgment to guide site investigation and remediation strategies, oversee field programs and data evaluation, prepare and review technical deliverables, and support regulatory and client communications. You will also provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior and mid-level staff while helping ensure projects are completed efficiently, safely, and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The position provides opportunities to work on a diverse range of projects involving, geologic and environmental investigations, conceptual site model development, remedial strategy and design, data evaluation and modelling, regulatory compliance and technical reporting.

Your key tasks and responsibilities for this role will be:

Lead and oversee geologic and site investigations, including Remedial Investigations, Feasibility Studies, Remedial Designs, Remedial Actions, and post-remediation OM&M; plan and oversee various drilling methodologies and investigation techniques, including monitoring well installations, packer testing, groundwater sampling, and vapor intrusion investigations.
Oversee and review detailed and accurate field and project documentation; manage and successfully track field and project activities related to scope, schedule, and budget.
Serve as a key technical point of contact for clients and project stakeholders, communicating investigation findings, technical recommendations, project status, and emerging issues; participate in client meetings and work collaboratively with LSRP and technical leads to develop practical solutions that meet project and client objectives.
Coordinate the development and finalization through final submission of technical documents, including regulatory reports, work plans, and biennial remedial action protectiveness submittals, pursuant to regulatory requirements; independently develop scopes of work and budgetary cost estimates and support initial project setup, invoicing, and project closeout.
Proactively communicate change management needs during project execution; provide technical guidance and mentorship to early-career and mid-level Geological Scientists and contribute to the development of team capabilities and technical best practices.

Qualifications

About you

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Geological Science, Environmental Science, or related field, with 5+ years of relevant experience.
Possession, eligibility, or demonstrated progress toward obtaining, a PG license and/or LSRP.
At a minimum, 40-Hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification and up-to-date 8-hour refresher; additional OSHA health and safety training and certifications are a plus.
Strong working knowledge of federal New York environmental and site remediation regulations, with demonstrated experience applying regulatory requirements to investigation and remediation projects.
Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, managing technical tasks, and communicating technical findings and recommendations to clients, regulators, and other project stakeholders; strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Meaningful, high-impact work
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Competitive compensation and benefits
Professional development and leadership opportunities
A collaborative and inclusive culture
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $81,515 – $101,891 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

Ready to join us?

new_jobs.description:
Overview

At UES, we’re a team of more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, geologists, inspectors, technicians, and drillers united by a shared purpose—to make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. As a national leader in geotechnical engineering, environmental consulting, and materials testing and inspection, we collaborate on transformative projects across transportation, energy, water, healthcare, and more. Learn more about the benefits of joining Team UES and our core values at careers.teamues.com.

Position Overview

Build Your Career in the Field

Are you someone who enjoys working outdoors, solving problems hands-on, and seeing the direct impact of your work? Join our team as a Field Technician I
and play an important role in projects that help build stronger communities, safer infrastructure, and a more sustainable environment.

This is an excellent opportunity for individuals looking to launch or grow a career in engineering support, construction materials testing, environmental services, and field inspections. You'll work alongside experienced professionals, receive industry-leading training, and gain valuable technical skills while contributing to meaningful projects across your region.

Learn More About The Role

UES Field Technician Video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDH-cBgmmwg

What You'll Do

As a Field Technician I, You'll Be Part Of a Collaborative Team Supporting a Variety Of Construction, Infrastructure, And Environmental Projects. Your Work May Include

Performing field inspections and testing at active project sites
Collecting environmental and construction-related samples
Supporting quality assurance efforts that help ensure project success
Working with engineers, project managers, and technical specialists
Operating field equipment and learning industry-standard testing methods
Helping maintain safety and quality standards on every project
Building technical expertise through on-the-job training and mentorship

Every day brings something different, offering exposure to a wide range of projects, technologies, and challenges.

What Makes You Successful

We're Looking For Individuals Who Are

Curious, motivated, and eager to learn
Comfortable working outdoors in varying weather conditions
Detail-oriented with a strong commitment to quality
Focused on safety and following best practices
Dependable, team-oriented, and professional
Strong problem-solvers who can adapt in fast-paced environments
Willing to travel to project sites as needed

Responsibilities

Conduct field and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, asphalt, aggregate, and other construction materials to verify compliance with project specifications, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
Properly collect, label, and transport samples from job sites to laboratories for further testing and analysis.
Ensure that project testing requirements are met and compliant with project specifications, requirements, and company policies or procedures.
Complete detailed reports, logs, and documentation of test results, ensuring accuracy and timely submission to project managers and stakeholders.
Ensure all testing equipment is properly maintained, and functioning correctly, following company and manufacturer guidelines.
Accurately document test results, observations, and site conditions, preparing and submitting timely and detailed reports, logs, and presentations in accordance with company standards.
Communicate effectively with dispatch, field supervisors, contractors, and project managers, providing real-time updates on job status, site conditions, and any issues encountered.
Adhere to project timelines and schedules, reporting to job sites on time and completing assignments within established deadlines.
Adapt to changing project requirements, schedules, and weather conditions, maintaining flexibility to support business needs.
Participate in ongoing training and certification programs, as required, to maintain technical proficiency and industry compliance.
Follow strict safety protocols and OSHA regulations to maintain a safe work environment, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and adherence to company and client safety guidelines.
Operate and maintain an assigned company vehicle, including scheduling routine maintenance (oil changes, tire checks, fluid levels) and ensuring general cleanliness inside and out.
Perform other duties as assigned to support project goals and company initiatives.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; vocational training or coursework in construction, engineering, geology, or a related field is a plus.
0-3 years of experience in a field-based, outdoor, or physically demanding role preferred (construction, materials testing, geotechnical, or related industry experience is a plus).
Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record; ability to operate company-assigned vehicles safely.
Industry certifications as applicable such as ACI Level 1 Concrete Testing, or ability to obtain within a specified time period.
Commitment to workplace safety, following OSHA standards and company safety policies, including the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Basic computer proficiency, including experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Field Data Collection (FDC) software or similar industry tools.
Mathematical skills sufficient to add, subtract, multiply, and divide into all units of measure using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
Ability to read, write, and interpret blueprints, procedures, manuals, technical documents, and reports related to drilling, safety, and project requirements.
Efficient time management, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to complete tasks efficiently and accurately.
Attention to detail to ensure accurate sample collection, testing procedures, and documentation.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively, demonstrating a strong work ethic and commitment to producing high-quality results.
Flexibility to work varying schedules, including early mornings, weekends, overtime, and potential overnight travel as project demands require.

Travel Requirements

This position requires extensive travel, approximately up to 70% of the time, in support of business

objectives and client engagements. Travel may be both scheduled and on short notice, depending on

project needs. Destinations typically include job sites, field locations, or regional offices, where work may be conducted in outdoor or operational environments. Adherence to all company safety protocols and use of PPE is required during travel and on-site work.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

This position primarily works in an outdoor work environment, regularly exposed to varying field conditions, including:

Sites that may not be accessible by vehicle, requiring travel on foot through wetlands, swamps, grasslands, fields, and other uneven or rugged terrain with natural and man-made obstacles such as sand, brush, and debris.
Moderate to loud noise levels, common in active construction and industrial environments.
Exposure to environmental elements including dirt, dust, sun, heat, humidity, and adverse weather conditions.

Ability to lift and/or carry 35 to 50 lbs. up to 75 feet, involving regular repetitive motion.
Ability to stand, walk, drive, and operate equipment for extended periods.
Frequent use of hands and arms for typing, handling tools, and operating equipment.
Ability to bend, twist, reach, stoop, pull, kneel, climb, balance, lift, carry, and push as required for fieldwork and inspections.

new_jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst, Lumina Data Platform
new_jobs.description:
Overview

We are building a cloud-native data platform that ingests, governs, and serves data to teams across the company. We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst who can turn that data into clear, trustworthy answers — and document it well enough that others can reuse the work. You will sit close to the platform and its consumers, analyzing data to drive decisions while writing the queries, definitions, and guides that make the platform easier for everyone to use.

This role blends deep analytical work with strong technical writing. You will not only produce analysis, you will document data sources, metrics, and how-to guidance so that self-service actually works. We move fast and use AI as a normal part of the job, so we want someone who reaches for those tools to raise the quality and speed of their work.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do

Deliver analysis that drives decisions — scope questions with stakeholders, pull and model data from the platform, and turn it into clear findings and recommendations.
Be the go-to expert on the platform's data — develop deep knowledge of the data model, the data it holds, and the platform's capabilities, and answer questions from consumers about what data exists, what it means, and how to use it.
Own metrics and definitions — define, validate, and maintain the key metrics teams rely on, and keep them consistent across the platform.
Write technical documentation — document data sources, schemas, metric definitions, and query patterns so consumers can find and trust the data without a meeting.
Enable self-service — build reusable queries, dashboards, and how-to guides that let other teams answer their own questions.
Safeguard data quality — profile new and existing sources, flag anomalies, and partner with data engineering to resolve issues at the source.
Be a bridge to the platform — translate consumer needs into feedback for the platform team, and help onboard teams onto new data as it lands.
Work AI-forward — use AI tools as a default part of how you analyze, draft SQL, summarize findings, and produce documentation — and share what works with the team.

Qualifications

What We're Looking For

5+ years in data analysis, business intelligence, or a similar role delivering analysis that shaped real decisions.
Strong SQL — you can independently query, join, and model data in a cloud warehouse; comfort with a scripting language such as Python is a plus.
Data platform fluency — hands-on understanding of modern cloud data architectures, data pipelines, and schemas; able to trace data from source to consumption, identify data issues, and partner effectively on technical solutions.
Technical writing skills — you write clear, well-organized documentation — data dictionaries, metric definitions, runbooks, and how-to guides — that non-experts can follow.
Rigor and clarity — you validate your numbers, explain your assumptions, and communicate findings simply to technical and non-technical audiences.
AI-forward mindset — you actively use AI tools to do your best work and raise your leverage, and you stay current as the tooling evolves.
US-based — authorized to work in the United States; this role is open to US-based candidates.

Nice to Have

Real estate / proptech experience — familiarity with property, leasing, or real estate data is desired but not required.
Experience standing up or maintaining a data catalog, data dictionary, or metrics layer.
Experience supporting internal consumers of a shared data platform.
Familiarity with dbt, version control, or documentation-as-code workflows.

How We'll Measure Success

Analysis that stakeholders act on, delivered accurately and on time.
A well-documented, trusted set of metrics and data sources that others reuse.
Growth in self-service — teams answering their own questions from your guides and queries.
Faster, higher-quality output through effective use of AI tools.

Salary And Benefits

RealPage provides a competitive salary package along with a comprehensive benefit plan that includes:

Health, dental, and vision insurance.
Retirement savings plan with company match.
Paid time off and holidays.
Professional development opportunities.
Performance-based bonus based on position.

This is a Fully Remote Job

About Our Client:

The organization operates within the cybersecurity sector, focusing on vulnerability management to enhance security program effectiveness. It addresses challenges related to data integrity and program performance measurement by transforming raw scan, asset, and remediation data into reliable metrics. This enables leadership and stakeholders to understand risk posture accurately and supports informed decision-making.

About the Opportunity:

The CYBER DATA ANALYST is responsible for managing the analytics, reporting, and data quality aspects of a vulnerability management program. This role involves developing trusted metrics and dashboards, utilizing AI-assisted tools to identify and correct data defects, and collaborating with operational teams to improve data processes. The position is impactful in shaping how the security program measures and reports on its performance and risks.

Manage monthly data-quality reporting to identify and track data-integrity issues.
Design and refine AI-assisted workflows for large-scale data defect detection and correction.
Maintain version-controlled libraries of prompts, scripts, and workflows for reproducibility.
Reconcile business intelligence reports with authoritative vulnerability scan data.
Verify and certify vulnerability and asset ownership through coordination with operational teams.
Develop new reports, metrics, scoring algorithms, and dashboards based on stakeholder needs.
Transition mature analytics products to operational teams with documentation and training.
Collaborate with operations to trace data defects to root causes and recommend process improvements.
Produce audit-ready documentation for regulatory and stakeholder review.
Support additional analytical, reporting, and program improvement initiatives as assigned.

Requirements:

Minimum of 1 year experience in data analysis, data science, business intelligence, security analytics, IT operations reporting, or related fields.
Ability to work with large and imperfect data sets, including data joining and reconciliation.
Proficiency in building reports and dashboards with data modeling and calculated measures.
Advanced Excel skills, including lookups, pivot tables, and conditional logic.
Experience leveraging AI tools for analytical and data remediation tasks with sound judgment.
Familiarity with cybersecurity concepts such as vulnerabilities, patching, CVEs, CVSS scoring, and risk fundamentals.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical and leadership audiences.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and SharePoint.
Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and ability to manage multiple tasks within deadlines.

Our Mission:
Hospital-Quality Care, Everywhere.

The healthcare industry still relies on faxes and phone tags to coordinate critical care for patients at home. We think patients and the clinicians who serve them deserve better than a system stuck in 1995.

Verse Medical is building the modern software infrastructure to make it happen. We're a well-funded Series C company (backed by General Catalyst, SignalFire, and Sapphire Ventures) on a mission to heal a fragmented system. Our platform connects the dots between providers, payors, and patients, ensuring people get the high-quality care they need, reliably and right where they live. We’re growing fast and looking for people who are driven by this mission to join us!

Our Values:
The Principles That Guide Us

Our values are the operating system for how we work together and with our partners. They aren't just words on a wall; they are the principles we bring to every decision, every day.

We are transparent, upfront and direct. We operate with honesty and clarity. We share information openly, the good and the bad, and believe that direct, respectful feedback is the foundation of trust and progress.
We value speed of iteration. We are building something new, which means we learn by doing. We prioritize rapid iteration and getting solutions into the hands of users, believing that progress is more valuable than perfection.
We give 110% effort, 30% of the time. We are passionate about our mission, and there are moments that require us to go the extra mile. We believe in focused intensity when it counts, balanced by a sustainable pace that keeps our team energized for the long run.
We empathize with customers to a fault. When our users face a problem, we own it. Instead of asking them to change, we ask ourselves, "How can we make this better?" We believe true innovation comes from deep empathy and a relentless focus on solving the real-world challenges of healthcare.

We’re hiring a Data Analyst
to turn Verse's data into decisions. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role where you'll partner directly with functional leaders to build the metrics, dashboards, and analyses that drive how the business operates. Not only are you offering the “what,” but also the “why” and the “what now,” translating messy, ambiguous business questions into clear, defensible, self-serve analytical assets.

If you enjoy high ownership, solving open-ended business problems with data, and having direct influence on a mission-driven company’s trajectory, this role is for you.

What You'll Achieve: A Glimpse into Your Contributions

Spearhead end-to-end analytics across business domains.
Understand trends in operational and customer data to influence how teams prioritize their own roadmaps
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Ops, Product, Leadership) to define new metrics, standardize reporting, and surface insights proactively.
Automate recurring reporting and manual data-quality checks using Python and SQL, reducing turnaround time on regular audits and deliverables.
Design and build algorithms/models (e.g., scoring, classification, similarity, or risk-adjustment models) that solve specific business problems, from provider mapping to fraud detection to cost-of-care scoring.

What You'll Bring: The Skills and Experience You’ll Leverage

We believe that diverse experiences and backgrounds lead to better solutions. While we have an idea of what will help someone succeed in this role, we are open to being convinced by your unique story and skills. If you believe you can achieve the outcomes above, we encourage you to apply.

3+ years of experience in data analysis, business intelligence, or analytics engineering, with experience owning reporting and metrics end-to-end.
Strong experience writing SQL and Python for analysis, automation, and lightweight modeling
Experience building and driving adoption of dashboards (Metabase, Looker Tableau, PowerBI, or similar)
Experience developing custom metrics, scoring algorithms, or classification models to solve specific business problems.
Experience performing exploratory analysis with minimal direction on ambiguous, open-ended business questions
Proactive communicator with experience working with stakeholders
Preferred: Experience with dbt modeling.
Preferred: Experience with Snowflake.
Preferred: Familiarity with healthcare or other regulated data (HIPAA compliance).
Preferred: Experience working closely with engineers to triage and resolve issues.

Competitive compensation.
Opportunities for rapid career advancement in a growing company.
100% premium coverage for health insurance.
401(k) with no matching at this time.

new_jobs.title: Lead Master Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Piper Companies
is seeking a Lead Master Data Analyst
to join a leading medical device manufacturing organization in King of Prussia, PA
. The Lead Master Data Analyst
will serve as a key supply chain and ERP/MRP subject matter expert, driving planning master data integrity, governance, and optimization initiatives across a global manufacturing network.

Responsibilities of the Lead Master Data Analyst:

Establish and enforce global governance standards for planning master data, ensuring consistency across manufacturing sites and regions.
Own and validate critical planning parameters including lead times, safety stock methodologies, lot sizes, BOM structures, sourcing rules, and capacity settings.
Serve as the ERP/MRP SME, investigating planning system anomalies and driving root-cause resolution for excess inventory, shortages, and scheduling disruptions.
Partner with Supply Chain, Operations, IT, and Planning teams to implement ERP enhancements, data harmonization initiatives, and process automation improvements.
Develop scalable master data frameworks supporting new product introductions (NPI), acquisitions, and business growth initiatives.
Build Power BI dashboards, audit controls, and exception reporting tools to improve planning performance, data quality, and inventory visibility.

Qualifications of the Lead Master Data Analyst:

8+ years of experience in supply chain planning, master data governance, ERP administration, or MRP systems within a manufacturing environment.
Strong hands-on experience with ERP platforms such as SAP, Oracle, or equivalent enterprise systems.
Deep understanding of MRP logic, planning parameter configuration, BOM management, inventory optimization, and capacity modeling.
Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations with a focus on supply chain data integrity and system governance.
Advanced analytical capabilities including Excel, Power BI, SQL, or related data management tools.
APICS CPIM/CSCP certification, Lean Six Sigma experience, and knowledge of regulated environments are highly preferred.

Compensation for the Lead Master Data Analyst includes:

Salary range: $85,000 - $90,000
Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and PTO

This job opens for applications on 10/07/2026. Applications for this job will be accepted for at least 30 days from the posting date.

new_jobs.title: Archaeological Field Technician
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is looking for a part-time junior-level Archaeological Field Technician based in Bloomington, MN.

Position Summary

The selected candidate will provide field support for archaeological surveys as part of a team or individually. The work will consist of project sites in the Midwest, Upper Midwest, and Northern Great Plains.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Perform field activities around various project sites, walking up to 10-15 miles per day.
Perform shovel testing and screening.
Conduct pedestrian surveys.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in anthropology or archaeology desired. In lieu of a degree, a minimum of 5 years of experience conducting advocational archaeology is required
1-5 years of relevant environmental experience.
Knowledge of Midwest and Great Plains Archaeology.
Currently reside in the Twin Cities Metro Area of Minnesota.
Strong communication skills (both written and verbal).
Strong team player with a collaborative mindset.
Strong time-management skills and ability to work on tasks as part of a larger project team.
Driving on a regular basis. Passing a motor vehicle record background check and maintaining a valid driver's license and good driving record is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Existing experience conducting pedestrian surveys and shovel tests.
Familiarity with maps and being able to navigate with maps and/or GPS.

Physical Requirements

Walk around project sites in all types of terrains for up to 10-15 miles per day.
Ability to carry up to 25 lbs. of equipment such as maps, shovels, GPS unit, field screening equipment and cameras during field work.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Field activities take place in a variety of weather conditions and can occur in remote locations and include areas of uneven terrain.
The work environment will consist of field work, with some field work requiring overnight stays.
Field work may occur in all seasons.

Additional Information

This part-time position requires 100% travel.
The work schedule is variable based on available fieldwork.
Travel requirements will include day-long projects and multi-day field projects out of town requiring overnight stays.
Travel requirements may include weekends.
Out-of-town field efforts range from 5 to 10 days but can be up to 12 days.
Typical break between mobilizations is 2 to 4 days, depending on duration of field efforts.
Must be able to drive on a regular basis. Passing a motor vehicle record background check and maintaining a valid driver's license and good driving record is required.

Life at Tetra Tech

The Perks Of Working At Tetra Tech Include

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits
Merit-based financial rewards
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth

Benefits

Tetra Tech offers a basic core medical plan and our 401k retirement plan for this position.

The rate of pay for this position is $23.00 - $28.00 per hour, depending on education, experience, skills, and location.

Health and safety play a vital role in our success. Tetra Tech’s employees work together to comply with all applicable health & safety practices and protocols, including any public health orders and regulations that are mandated by local, state, provincial, federal, and international authorities as well as client and project requirements.

Qualifications - External

About Tetra Tech:

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. Our 25,000 employees work together to provide clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

LinkedIn: @TetraTechCareers

X (Twitter): @TetraTechJobs

Please no phone calls or agencies.

new_jobs.title: Project Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Amentum is a global leader in advanced engineering and innovative solutions, supporting critical missions across defense, intelligence, energy, and civilian sectors. Our people are our competitive advantage, driven by purpose, collaboration, and a commitment to delivering excellence for our customers and communities.

We are seeking a Project Coordinator to join Amentum’s Advanced Solutions Group. Candidates may be based at our Tullahoma, TN; Farmington Hills, MI; or Greenville, SC office.

Our Advanced Solutions Group delivers the design, construction, and operation of unique and complex research and development facilities across the nuclear, automotive, motorsports, defense, and aerospace industries. Our team has supported an impressive range of clients, including Audi, Boeing, BMW, Fiat Chrysler, Ford, Honda, General Motors, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, U.S. Department of Energy, Volkswagen, and organizations throughout North America, Europe, and Asia.

Essential Responsibilities:

Support Project Managers with project planning, scheduling, cost estimates, specifications, requirements, deliverables, and team communications.
Coordinate workflows with engineering teams and functional groups, including project accounting, project controls, and project administration, to ensure information is communicated in accordance with the project control plan.
Track project progress, resource usage, estimates to complete (ETCs), change requests, pricing, and client-side project tracking deliverables; identify problem areas and recommend corrective actions.
Support procurement activities by vetting potential suppliers, coordinating bidding, assisting with subcontract and major vendor contracts, coordinating change orders, and providing feedback on supplier performance.
Interface effectively with customers, internal resources and functional groups, project teams, and external suppliers.
Assist in developing new business opportunities and gathering information needed to support project estimates and planning.
Support project and process quality audits, track and assist with the disposition of non-conforming products, and recommend opportunities for process improvement.
Interpret internal and external business issues, consider multiple perspectives, recommend best practices, and assist in resolving project delivery issues using established solutions and procedures.
Balance technical quality with cost and schedule requirements while maintaining an effective interface between the client and project team.
Manage projects of limited scope within contractual cost and schedule requirements, including reviewing documentation and deliverables for quality and quantity.
Work independently with guidance in the most complex or technical situations while following established deadlines, priorities, and limits of authority, with project progress reviewed by higher management.

Required Qualifications:

US citizenship is required to comply with government customer requirements and/or applicable government regulations.
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university and a minimum of 5 years of technical project experience, such as engineering or construction. Advanced degrees may substitute for years of engineering experience.
Demonstrated performance on assignments of increasing responsibility.
Comprehensive depth and/or breadth of expertise in capital expenditure project processes and organizational management, including marketing, design, procurement, fabrication and installation, and turnover processes.
Familiarity with project scheduling tools, such as Microsoft Project, as well as procurement processes and project management tools.
Strong communication skills, both in person and virtually through platforms such as Microsoft Teams.

Preferred Qualifications:

Familiarity with contracting specification processes and assembling procurement packages based on AIA MasterSpec or USG SpecsIntact.
Familiarity with financial/procurement systems such as PeopleSoft experience.

Description of Work Environment:

Work will mainly be performed in an inside-office environment.
Minimal travel to customer sites may be required.

This is a workforce planning requisition, we will be considering candidates at all levels for contingent and funded openings.

Compensation Details:

75,000 - 115,000

The compensation range or hourly rate listed for this position is provided as a good-faith estimate of what the company intends to offer for this role at the time this posting was issued. Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as job responsibilities, education, experience, skills, internal equity, market data, applicable collective bargaining agreements, and relevant laws.

Benefits Overview:

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to support you and your priorities. Offerings include:

Health, dental, and vision insurance
Paid time off and holidays
Retirement benefits (including 401(k) matching)
Educational reimbursement
Parental leave
Employee stock purchase plan
Tax-saving options
Disability and life insurance
Pet insurance

Note: Benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and applicable agreements. Positions governed by a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), the McNamara-O'Hara Service Contract Act (SCA), or other employment contracts may include different provisions/benefits.

About Us

Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Divcon

delivers fully integrated automation solutions nationwide that optimize performance, energy efficiency, and reliability across HVAC, lighting, power monitoring, and mission-critical systems. Leveraging advanced technologies - including Allen-Bradley PLCs, Ignition SCADA, and Delta DDC systems - we combine deep technical expertise with field-tested execution to deliver precise, scalable, and high-performance solutions.

About The Role

The Project Coordinator

is a project delivery support role designed to assist Project Managers in the successful execution of data center controls construction projects. This position provides administrative coordination, documentation management, schedule tracking, financial support, and cross-functional communication to ensure projects are executed efficiently and in accordance with company standards.

The Project Coordinator contributes to project success by maintaining documentation workflows, supporting cost and schedule tracking, coordinating vendors and field teams, and assisting with internal and client communication.

This is an onsite role in Irving, TX.

Key Responsibilities

Project Coordination & Execution

Support Project Managers in coordinating day-to-day execution of data center controls projects.
Assist in updating project schedules, track milestones, and identify potential risks or delays.
Coordinate internal teams, subcontractors, and vendors to support timely project delivery.
Assist with mobilization planning, site access documentation, and workforce logistics.
Support preparation of project status reports and internal dashboards.

Documentation & Controls

Manage document control processes, including submittals, RFIs, change logs, drawings, contracts, and closeout documents.
Maintain accurate and organized project files in project management, accounting, and document systems.
Track submittals and RFIs to ensure timely processing and follow-up.
Prepare meeting agendas, capture minutes, and track follow-up actions.
Update project management systems with current status notes, documentation, and dependencies.

Client & Stakeholder Support

Assist Project Managers with communication workflows and documentation required by clients.
Support coordination between engineering, procurement, accounting, and field teams.
Maintain action item logs and ensure timely follow-through on assigned tasks.

Cost, Billing & Administrative Support

Assist with budget tracking, cost coding, and invoice support.
Track purchase orders, subcontractor pay applications, vendor invoices, and material receipts.
Support preparation and tracking of change orders and associated documentation.
Coordinate with accounting to ensure accurate billing and job cost reporting.
Monitor committed costs versus budget and escalate discrepancies to the Project Manager.

Field &

Closeout

Support

Track daily reports and assist in compiling project progress documentation.
Support workforce planning documentation and field reporting processes.
Assist in tracking punch-list items and project closeout requirements.
Help assemble O&M manuals and closeout packages.
Archive project records in accordance with company standards.

Qualifications

Required

2+ years of project coordination or project administration experience in construction or related industries.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
High attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel required).
Experience with project management or accounting platforms.

Preferred

Experience supporting MEP, controls, building automation, or data center construction projects.
Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Business, or related field.
Basic understanding of construction financial processes including budgets, cost codes, and change orders.
Experience with platforms such as Procore, Monday.com, Sage Intacct, Foundation, or similar systems.

Physical Requirements

Sit and/or stand for extended periods (typically 6-8 hours per day) while performing computer-based tasks and facility support tasks.
Use hands and fingers to operate standard office equipment, including computers, keyboards, mice, telephones, scanners and printers.
Occasionally stand, walk, bend, stoop, or reach to access filing cabinets, retrieve documents, or attend meetings.
Lift, carry, push, or pull light objects and materials weighing up to 20-25 pounds (e.g., boxes of files or office supplies).
Have sufficient vision (with or without correction) to read computer screens, printed documents, and small print; and sufficient hearing to communicate effectively by phone and in person.
Work in a typical indoor office environment with moderate noise levels from office equipment, conversations, and occasional interruptions.

Opportunities for Growth Hands-on training and career advancement in an exploding data-center industry.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

new_jobs.title: Project Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Summary

Advanced Technology Systems Company (ATSC) is looking for a full-time, on-site Project Coordinator/Scheduler located in Gilbert, AZ. ATSC has a very robust benefit plan to include medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance and 401K plan.

Job Description

Supports effective management of ongoing programs and serves as liaison between Program Management, planning, project team, and line management. Reviews status of programs and budgets; manages schedules, prepares status reports, and CDRL’s. Assesses program issues and proposes resolutions to meet productivity, quality, and client-satisfaction goals and objectives. Develops mechanisms for monitoring program progress and for intervention and problem solving with Program Managers, other functional managers, and customers. Responsible for ensuring contract requirements and subcontractor responsibilities are being accomplished including working on the definition and implementation of program planning techniques to provide visibility on the contract. Responsibilities may include developing budgets and schedules to meet contractual/program requirements for an assigned portion of a program, decomposing program plan requirements, and monitoring and reporting performance against plans to ensure that contractual, cost and schedule objectives are met.

Knowledge/Skills And Ability

Frequent use and application of industry practices, techniques, and standards. General application of concepts and principles. Receives assignments in the form of objectives and establishes goals to meet outlined objectives.

Problem Complexity

Participates in the development of solutions to a variety of problems moderate in scope and complexity. Often refers to policies, procedures and practices for guidance.

Freedom To Act

Works under general direction on routine work but personal ownership of responsibilities is expected to meet the requirements of the program. May receive detailed instructions on new projects or assignments. Follows and helps establish and improve procedures. Work is reviewed for soundness of judgment, overall adequacy and accuracy.

Impact

Contributes to the completion of organizational projects/goals and success is evaluated on value/efficiencies added to the program.

Liason

Frequent internal company and external contacts. Represents organization on specific projects.

Required Qualifications

3+ years project/program management support experience.

Advanced user of Microsoft Excel, Power Point, Word and Project.
Advanced expertise in MS Project.
Experience developing and maintaining detailed project schedules using Microsoft Project.
Experience developing and maintaining resources loaded with Integrated Master Schedules.
Experience working closely with program management, technical teams, and finance to ensure integrated schedule alignment, resource tracking, and milestone forecasting.
Knowledge and experience delivery Integrated Master Schedules in accordance with GAO Schedule Assessment Guide, December 22nd, 2015, GAO-16-89G and the PMOD Scheduling Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
Detail-oriented, eager to learn and requires minimal supervision.
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Active DOD/DHS clearance is a plus.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

Work is typically performed in an office setting.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, sit, bend, demonstrate manual dexterity, climb stairs, talk, hear and see.
Must have the ability to lift 15-25 pounds.
Must be able to read, write and speak English.
